answer: Identity slots open on a spiral: each new registration must bond more than the last, so the thousandth fake costs a thousand times the first. Bonds are slashable when two attestations from one operator contradict. An attacker must lock real capital, wait out the tier delay, and risk total loss; honest agents climb to the summit on unbroken history, so faking never pays. At the zenith only a handful of bonded identities can clear.
